content: Protein restriction has been a common therapeutic approach for patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) for some time. However, its specific effects on delaying the progression to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) in children, as well as its influence on growth and nutritional status, remain uncertain. The objective of this study was to evaluate whether a protein-restricted diet is effective in delaying the initiation of maintenance dialysis and in maintaining adequate nutrition in children with CKD. The search for relevant studies included databases such as the Cochrane Renal Group Trials Register, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE, and EMBASE. Additionally, reference lists from nephrology textbooks, review articles, and other pertinent studies were examined. The inclusion criteria for the analysis were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared unrestricted protein diets with protein-restricted diets (restricted to safe levels as recommended by the World Health Organization) in children. The studies had to have a follow-up period of at least six months. Two independent authors selected the studies for inclusion. Statistical analyses were conducted using a random-effects model. For dichotomous outcomes, results were expressed as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). For continuous outcomes, the mean difference (MD) was used to assess the effects of treatment. Two studies involving a total of 250 children were identified. Of these, 124 children were assigned to a protein-restricted diet, while 126 children followed a control diet. The analysis revealed no significant differences between the two groups in terms of renal-related deaths (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.54 to 2.33), progression of kidney disease as measured by creatinine clearance at two years (MD 1.47, 95% CI -1.19 to 4.14), or growth outcomes (weight: MD -0.13, 95% CI -1.10 to 0.84; height: MD -1.99, 95% CI -4.84 to 0.86). The authors concluded that reducing protein intake does not appear to have a significant effect on delaying the progression to ESKD in children with CKD.
